## Context / Problem

`_inherited_child_impact` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py:241, ticket 3e4b) lets a
container inherit its direct children's declared `file_impact` as its drift scope, under a
POISON RULE: any non-closed child with an empty `file_impact` collapses the union to `{}`, and
the container falls back to whole-HEAD invalidation. The rule is right for silence and wrong
for an explicit claim — one genuinely-no-file-impact child (a coordination child, an
operator-action child)
currently discards every sibling's careful declaration and makes the parent re-review on any
commit in the repo. `p9_file_impact_coverage` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_lint.py:267)
names that child as a poisoner for the same reason.

With the tri-state from S1 [rebar:1934-63dd-4be9-4c48] and the scope kinds from S2 [rebar:749c-7546-6fe3-4d27], both
can distinguish the two cases.

## Approach

Change the poison test from "empty `file_impact`" to "UNDECLARED file-impact scope". A non-closed
direct child is then one of three things:

- `paths` → contributes its paths (unchanged);
- `none` → NEUTRAL: contributes nothing and does not poison — its truthful claim is that no
  file of the repo is in its scope, which adds nothing to the union and removes nothing from
  its precision;
- `undeclared` → poisons, as today (a partial union is fail-open for unknown scope).

`_inherited_child_impact` returns the union as now, but the caller needs to distinguish "empty
because every live child declared none" from "empty because there are no children" — the first
is scope `none`, the second leaves the container on its own declaration. The function
therefore returns a small result carrying both the path set and whether inheritance was
EFFECTIVE and all-none, and `dependency_hashes` / the S2 scope classifier consume that:

- container with any `paths` child → deps = union (scope `paths`);
- container whose non-closed children ALL declare `none`, and whose own impact is `none` or
  empty → scope `none`;
- container with an undeclared live child → deps as today (scope `unscoped` unless the
  container's own file_impact or citations scope it).

Closed children keep today's semantics: they neither contribute nor poison.

`p9_file_impact_coverage` follows the same rule: a LEAF with an explicit `none` PASSES with
coverage recording the declared kind; a CONTAINER's poisoning list counts only undeclared
children. The advisory text for a still-undeclared leaf gains the `--none` remedy alongside
`set_file_impact`, so the coaching names both exits.

**Integration ownership.** S3 owns the container handshake: it passes `container_all_none=_inherited_child_impact(...).all_none` into `classify_file_scope` introduced by S2 at the `dependency_hashes`/manifest call site. S2 owns explicit leaf `none`; S3 owns promotion of an all-none live-child container to effective scope `none`. S3 runs after S4 so its `orchestrator.py` edit incorporates the S4 `applies(..., file_impact_scope=...)` signature rather than racing the shared file.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py` — `_inherited_child_impact` tri-state result and its
  use in `dependency_hashes` / the scope classifier added in S2.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_lint.py` — `p9_file_impact_coverage` leaf + container rules
  and advisory text.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py` — confirm the child states fetched for P5/P8
  (line ~207) carry `file_impact_scope`; extend the projection if the fetch is field-limited.

Out of scope: the write surface (S1), the manifest/validity plumbing itself (S2), the review
criterion (S4).

## Testing

- `_inherited_child_impact` unit table: children ∈ {paths, none, undeclared, closed-anything}
  in the combinations that matter — paths+none → the paths union; all-none → empty-and-all-none;
  paths+undeclared → poisoned; none+closed-undeclared → still all-none (a closed child never
  poisons).
- End-to-end scope test: a container with one paths child and one none child signs an
  attestation scoped to the paths child's files, and a commit touching an UNRELATED file does
  not invalidate it, while a commit touching the declared file does.
- P9 table: leaf/none → pass; leaf/undeclared → advisory (unchanged); container with a none
  child and no undeclared child → pass; container with an undeclared child → advisory naming
  only that child.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A container with children `{A: paths, B: none}` inherits exactly A's paths; the signed
      dependency map contains A's files and nothing else (checked: unit test over
      `_inherited_child_impact` plus a `dependency_hashes` assertion).
- [ ] That container's attestation survives a commit to a file declared by NO child, and is
      invalidated by a commit to A's declared file (checked: `compute_validity` test).
- [ ] A container whose non-closed children ALL declare `none` is classified scope `none` and
      survives an unrelated commit (checked: scope-classifier + validity test).
- [ ] A container with one UNDECLARED non-closed child is still poisoned to the whole-HEAD
      fallback (checked: unchanged expectation in the same table).
- [ ] P9 passes for a leaf declaring `none` and still advises a leaf that declared nothing,
      with the advisory naming the `--none` remedy (checked: det_lint test asserting the
      result status and the remedy string).
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the full test suite pass.
